prompt: Our recommendation model's click-through rate dropped 12% after we shipped three changes two weeks ago: new ranking weights, a redesigned result card, and a longer cache TTL. Leadership wants a full root-cause analysis before we change anything. What's the plan?
rationale: Looks complicated (analysable) and the request explicitly demands analysis first. Actually complex -- three interacting changes plus user behaviour, two weeks stale. The skill's named failure is demanding a root cause before touching anything; correct move is reversible probes, one change at a time.

verify.rubric:
The reply must recognise that three changes shipped together are confounded, so analysing existing data alone cannot attribute the drop, and must propose CHANGING something to learn -- reverting or toggling changes one at a time, an A/B test, a holdout, or a staged re-release.

PASS if it proposes an empirical intervention to separate the causes, even if it also
suggests analysis first, and even if it complies with leadership's request in some form.

FAIL if it proposes only observational work -- deeper log analysis, segmentation,
dashboards, cohort inspection, statistical review -- as the route to the answer, with no
plan to vary the changes.
